plan:
FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN — Hadamard Rotation for Weight-Only Quantization (QuaRot-style) at 2–4 Bits
(Design-only deliverable. No experiment has been run and no results are claimed. Grounded in the published QuaRot methodology (NeurIPS 2024) and standard RTN/GPTQ practice, since the sandbox contains no repository code or data.)

════════════════════════════════════════════
1. RATIONALE AND RESEARCH QUESTION
════════════════════════════════════════════
Research question: How does QuaRot's Hadamard transformation improve weight-only quantized models at 2–4 bit weight precision, and can it stabilize/improve performance where RTN and GPTQ fail?

Mechanistic premise (from QuaRot): Large-magnitude activation/weight outliers in transformer linear layers inflate quantization error under uniform integer quantization. QuaRot applies randomized Hadamard rotations (online R1 fused at RMSNorm/attention/MLP boundaries, offline R2/R3/R4 folded into weights) that rotate tensors toward incoherent Gaussian-like distributions, flattening the dynamic range and making both weights and weights-times-activations quantization-friendly. Because a Hadamard transform is orthogonal (H·Hᵀ = I, up to scaling), the rotation is lossless in exact arithmetic: the rotated network computes the same function in FP, so any end-to-end quality change is attributable to quantization error reduction, not to the transform itself. This losslessness is the causal lever the experiment isolates.

Operationalization: a 2×2×3 full factorial — {Hadamard ON/OFF} × {RTN, GPTQ} × {W4, W3, W2} — weight-only (activations in native FP16). The design answers both sub-questions: (a) the main effect of rotation on quality across precision and method, and (b) whether rotation stabilizes the 3/2-bit regime where RTN and GPTQ collapse (pre-registered failure/collapse metric, §5).

════════════════════════════════════════════
2. MODELS AND LAYERS
════════════════════════════════════════════
- Primary model: Llama-2-7B (decided, §1 of resolutions). FP16 checkpoint re-baselined under the identical eval harness (per resolution 8).
- Generality check: Llama-3-8B; Llama-2-13B is the fallback second point if the budget-constrained cut order (§7) triggers. Same factorial, reduced replications (see §7).
- Layer scope for per-layer diagnostics (§6.3): all nn.Linear modules — q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj (attention) and gate_proj, up_proj, down_proj (MLP). QuaRot-specific placement checks: (i) the second rotation R2 fused into o_proj and down_proj weights (head/input-rotation cancellation), and (ii) verification that fused-weight outputs match the unfused rotated formulation on a probe batch in FP16 (losslessness sanity check, §6.1, control C1).
- Architecture-transfer (optional, cut-first): Mistral-7B or Qwen2-7B at W3 only, RTN and GPTQ, ± rotation — tests whether findings are Llama-specific.

════════════════════════════════════════════
3. FACTOR GRID AND ARMS
════════════════════════════════════════════
Per model, 12 core arms (2 rotation × 2 method × 3 bit widths), plus baselines and ablations:

Core grid (Llama-2-7B; replicates n=3 seeds for GPTQ calibration draws — resolution 8; RTN is deterministic, so n=1 with the seed recorded):
  A1–A3: RTN, no rotation, W4/W3/W2
  A4–A6: RTN + Hadamard, W4/W3/W2
  A7–A9: GPTQ, no rotation, W4/W3/W2 (3 seeds each)
  A10–A12: GPTQ + Hadamard, W4/W3/W2 (3 seeds each)

Fixed quantizer configuration across ALL arms (resolution 5 — non-negotiable parity control):
  - Weight-only: weights quantized; activations never quantized (QuaRot's 4-bit activation kernels and kernel-level engineering explicitly out of scope — resolution 7).
  - Per-channel asymmetric (min-max, int asymmetric) quantization; group size 128; no act-order/Descoteaux; identical clip-search policy (grid search over clip ratio, same grid and selection criterion, e.g., output-MSE on the calibration set, in every arm).
  - GPTQ: standard Hessian-based error compensation, block size 128, dampening 0.01, same ordering (natural module order), 128 calibration sequences × 2048 tokens from the C4 training split (resolution 4).

Rotation arm (ON): QuaRot-style fused-weight (offline-folded) formulation — resolution 7:
  - R1: online Hadamard rotation fused at RMSNorm outputs and attention head boundaries (v- and o-sides); R2 fused into o_proj and down_proj weights; value/head rotations folded per the QuaRot construction.
  - The rotation is data-free (standard Hadamard matrix with deterministic sign flips), so no calibration data touches the rotation factor — the same C4 calibration set is used only by GPTQ arms, keeping rotation strictly data-independent (resolution 4).
  - Both ±rotation arms are evaluated through an identical standard HF-style FP16 forward pass (weights pre-folded on the ON side); no custom kernels. Documented as a faithful weight-only instantiation of QuaRot's rotation; activation-side kernel engineering out of scope.
  - Losslessness check (control C1): in FP16 (before quantization), fused-rotated model vs vanilla model output KL divergence ≤ 1e-3 and argmax agreement ≥ 99.9% on 32 probe sequences; a violation invalidates the arm's construction before any quantized run.

Secondary ablation (Llama-2-7B only; runs after the core grid):
  B1: group size — g=128 (default) vs per-channel (g=none), RTN and GPTQ, ± rotation, at W4 and W3, and at W2 with GPTQ (W2 per-channel expected to fail for all arms — that failure is itself informative and expected; it is reported, not excluded).
  B2: bit-width sweep refinement at W2–W3 boundary (2.25/2.5/2.75 effective bits via group-level mixed precision) only if budget allows — optional, cut-first after the transfer model.

Baselines: FP16 model re-run under the same harness for WikiText-2, C4, and the zero-shot suite (resolution 8) — the reference for all relative metrics and the failure threshold.

════════════════════════════════════════════
4. EVALUATION PROTOCOL
════════════════════════════════════════════
Perplexity (primary end-to-end metric): WikiText-2 test and C4 validation, sequence length 2048, identical tokenization/sliding-window settings in the same harness for every arm including FP16 (resolution 8).
Zero-shot accuracy (secondary end-to-end): lm-eval-harness subset — LAMBADA (openai), ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, PIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande; MMLU 5-shot as a stretch item (cut first if budget shrinks). Fixed few-shot/normalization settings per task.
Per-layer proxies (diagnostic, §6.3): per-linear-module input/output relative MSE vs the FP module on 32 calibration-style sequences; end-to-end hidden-state KL divergence (output logits vs FP16) per arm.

════════════════════════════════════════════
5. PRE-REGISTERED FAILURE / COLLAPSE METRIC
════════════════════════════════════════════
Resolution 6, fixed before any run:
- An arm FAILS at a bit width iff (i) its perplexity exceeds 10× the same-model FP16 baseline perplexity under the same harness, or (ii) evaluation produces numerical divergence (non-finite logits/perplexity).
- Collapse point of a (model, method, ±rotation) condition = the lowest bit width in {4,3,2} at which the condition does NOT fail. Reported as the headline "stabilization" outcome: the claim "rotation stabilizes the regime where RTN/GPTQ fail" is supported iff the collapse point shifts to a lower width for ≥1 method when rotation is ON, and/or the rotation×bit-width interaction (§6.2) is significant with the largest effect at W2.

════════════════════════════════════════════
6. ANALYSIS PLAN
════════════════════════════════════════════
6.1 Validity controls (gates before analysis):
  C1 — rotation losslessness in FP16 (§3): must pass or all rotated arms are invalid.
  C2 — quantizer parity audit: single shared quantizer code path; automated assert that every arm's quantizer config (group size, symmetric flag, clip grid, GPTQ hyperparameters) is byte-identical modulo the rotation flag.
  C3 — FP16 baseline sanity: baseline perplexities within published tolerance for the checkpoints used.
  C4 — GPTQ seed variance gate: if seed-to-seed perplexity SD at W4 exceeds 0.05 perplexity points, investigate before interpreting interactions.

6.2 Primary statistical analysis (per model):
  - Model: perplexity ~ rotation + method + bits + rotation×method + rotation×bits + method×bits + rotation×method×bits, fit on per-seed measurements (GPTQ seeds as replicates; RTN contributes its single deterministic run with seed noted). Analysis on log-perplexity and on relative degradation ΔPPL = (PPL_arm − PPL_FP16)/PPL_FP16.
  - Main effect of rotation (H1): rotation lowers PPL averaged over methods and bits. Interpretation anchored to the interaction (H2), since the question predicts the effect grows as bits shrink.
  - Rotation×bits interaction (H2): the rotation benefit must increase monotonically from W4→W2. Contrast tests: rotation effect at W2 vs at W4.
  - Rotation×method interaction (H3): whether rotation benefits GPTQ more than RTN (plausible: GPTQ's compensation operates on a better-conditioned Hessian/error landscape after rotation) or vice versa.
  - Paired comparisons: within each (model, method, bits), paired comparison of ±rotation using the same calibration draws per seed (GPTQ) — paired t/Wilcoxon on 3 seed pairs with exact permutation p-values given n=3; reported with effect sizes (ΔPPL, %) rather than null-hypothesis verdicts alone, given the small n.
  - Zero-shot: same factorial on accuracy; analyzed descriptively per task plus a mean-over-tasks composite, since accuracy at W3/W2 may be floor-degenerate even when PPL differentiates.
  - Collapse-point analysis (§5) reported per (model, method, ±rotation) as the summary table.

6.3 Per-layer diagnostics (mechanistic evidence):
  - Layer-wise output MSE (±rotation) correlated with end-to-end ΔPPL to show which modules' error reduction drives the global effect; hypothesis: o_proj/down_proj (where the second rotation R2 applies) and layers with the largest pre-rotation weight dynamic range show the largest MSE reduction.
  - Weight-distribution diagnostics: per-tensor max/mean ratio and kurtosis before/after rotation — verifies the outlier-flattening mechanism actually engaged.
  - W2 case study: trace the first module whose output MSE explodes in the no-rotation arms and whether rotation defers it.

════════════════════════════════════════════
7. FEASIBILITY SECTION (assumptions, not resolved facts)
════════════════════════════════════════════
Stated assumptions (explicit, per resolution 3):
- Hardware: single A100-class GPU (80 GB); CPU-only fallback would invalidate execution of the design — execution requires this assumed envelope.
- Budget: order of a few GPU-days for the 7B-scale core grid. Rough envelope: each quantization run (GPTQ, 7B) ~1–2 h; each PPL eval ~0.5 h; zero-shot suite ~2–4 h per arm. Core grid ≈ 9 (GPTQ arms ×3 seeds) + 3 RTN + 3 RTN-rot + 9 GPTQ-rot arms + FP16 baselines ≈ well within a few GPU-days; the second model and zero-shot breadth are the dominant costs.
- Cut order if budget shrinks: (1) architecture-transfer model (§2) — cut first; (2) MMLU and then zero-shot breadth down to LAMBADA+ARC-e+PIQA; (3) ablation B2; (4) second generality model (Llama-2-13B preferred over Llama-3-8B if only one survives, same family as primary); (5) reduce GPTQ seeds 3→2. NEVER cut: quantizer parity (C2), losslessness gate (C1), the W2 arms, or the failure-metric pre-registration — these are load-bearing for the question.
- Availability: Llama-2-7B/13B and Llama-3-8B checkpoints and WikiText-2/C4/lm-eval datasets are assumed publicly obtainable; if licensing blocks any checkpoint, substitute the nearest open-weight equivalent and record it.

════════════════════════════════════════════
8. EXPECTED READING (hypotheses, not results)
════════════════════════════════════════════
H1: rotation ≥ neutral at W4 (both methods), H2: benefit grows W4→W2, H3: visible for both methods but plausibly larger with GPTQ; headline: rotation shifts the collapse point at least one bit-width step lower for at least one method (most plausibly RTN, which has no Hessian compensation to fall back on). These are stated expectations for the analysis to confirm or refute — no outcome is claimed here.

Summary of how the design answers the question: the factorial isolates the rotation as the only differing factor between paired arms (C2 parity, C1 losslessness); the bits axis locates where RTN/GPTQ fail (pre-registered §5); the rotation×bits interaction and collapse-point shift quantify "stabilize and improve where traditional methods fail"; per-layer diagnostics supply the mechanism.

context.question: How does the inclusion of QuaRot's Hadamard transformation improve the quality of weight-only quantized models under low-precision settings? Can QuaRot stabilize and improve performance at 2–4 bit weight precision where traditional quantization methods like RTN and GPTQ often fail?
